summary: Checked the fix for the login 404 error. The mobile backend (https://job-sheet-hub-2.preview.emergentagent.com) is STILL DOWN: POST /api/auth/login returns HTTP 404 'text/plain' '404 page not found', but the CORS headers are present (access-control-allow-origin: *), so the browser can read the response. On both frontend hosts (desktop 1920x1080 and mobile 390x844), login with admin@officina.it / Admin2026! now shows data-testid=login-error 'Server dell'app mobile non raggiungibile. Riattiva l'app mobile e riprova.' instead of 'Errore 404'. The empty-fields check ('Inserisci email e password') also works. The successful login, dashboard-stats and wrong-password ('Email o password non corretti') checks could NOT be run because the mobile backend is down.

critical.issue: The mobile app's backend is asleep and returns a plain-text 404 for every request. Nobody can log in until the mobile app is reactivated. This is outside the web app's codebase.

integration_issues.issue: When the app starts, any failure of /auth/me (including the backend being down) calls setToken(null). Users get silently logged out whenever the mobile backend sleeps. It would be better to clear the token only on a 401.

action_items: Tell the user to reactivate/wake the mobile app job-sheet-hub-2. The web code works, but the backend it calls is down.
Optional: in auth.jsx, clear the token only when /auth/me returns 401, not on network errors or a sleeping backend.
critical_code_review_comments: api.js: any non-OK response that is not JSON is treated as 'server non raggiungibile'. That fits proxy/ingress 404/502/503 errors. FastAPI errors are JSON, so the backend's detail message is kept.
auth.jsx: the catch-all around /auth/me logs users out on transient errors.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of the scenarios that could be tested (down-backend message, empty-field validation); success-path and wrong-password scenarios blocked

context_for_next_testing_agent: First curl POST https://job-sheet-hub-2.preview.emergentagent.com/api/auth/login. If it returns JSON, test a successful login leading to dashboard-stats, and a wrong password showing 'Email o password non corretti'. Shared real DB: do not modify data.
rca of the issue: The user's 'Errore 404' came from the mobile backend's preview environment being asleep. The ingress returns a text/plain 404 for /api/*. Before the fix, api.js showed a generic 'Errore {status}'. Now non-JSON errors map to a clear Italian message. To fully fix it, the mobile app has to be woken up.
